help.title: Why position size matters more than the entry
help.idea: First decide how much you are willing to lose, then let the math set the position size — not the other way round. That way no single trade can do outsized damage to the account.
help.formulaExplain: The numerator is how much money you risk. The denominator is how much you lose per unit if the stop is hit. Dividing gives the number of units that keeps the risk fixed — wherever the stop is.
help.step2: Choose the risk per trade. 0.25%–1.5% is the disciplined range; 1% is a good starting point.
help.step3: Enter the entry price and the stop-loss price — the real levels from your plan, not rough guesses.
help.step4: Read “Position size” — that is the number of shares, units or contracts for the order.
help.principle1: Risk management before returns — surviving every market regime is the condition for profit.
help.principle2: Process, not prediction — a fixed risk per trade turns trading into a repeatable process.
help.principle3: No signals — this tool doesn’t tell you what to buy, only how much once you already have a plan.
help.disclaimer: This is educational material and is not investment advice.
